meta.about: Curated reference for food additives (INS / E numbers). ADI = acceptable daily intake in mg per kg of body weight per day. Primary sources: JECFA (FAO/WHO) evaluations, EFSA re-evaluations, IARC classifications, FSSAI Food Products Standards and Food Additives Regulations, US FDA. 'concern' is this app's plain-language summary, not a regulatory status.
meta.review_required: Have a qualified food scientist or nutritionist re-check every entry against the original JECFA/EFSA/FSSAI documents before a public launch, and on a schedule after that. Regulatory status changes.

additives.name: Curcumin
additives.note: Natural yellow colour from turmeric.

additives.name: Tartrazine
additives.note: Synthetic yellow dye. A UK study linked mixtures of this and similar dyes to increased hyperactivity in some children; a small number of people react to it.
regulatory: EU: foods containing it must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

additives.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
additives.note: Synthetic orange-yellow dye; one of the dyes in the UK hyperactivity study.
regulatory: EU: warning label about activity and attention in children required.

additives.name: Carmines (cochineal)
additives.note: Red colour made from cochineal insects, so it is not vegetarian. A few people are allergic to it.

additives.name: Carmoisine (Azorubine)
additives.note: Synthetic red dye; one of the dyes in the UK hyperactivity study.
regulatory: EU: warning label about activity and attention in children required.
Not permitted as a food colour in the USA.

additives.name: Ponceau 4R
additives.adi_source: JECFA (EFSA set a lower ADI of 0.7)
additives.note: Synthetic red dye; one of the dyes in the UK hyperactivity study.
regulatory: EU: warning label about activity and attention in children required.
Not permitted as a food colour in the USA.

additives.name: Erythrosine
additives.note: Synthetic pink-red dye. Caused thyroid tumours in male rats at high doses; the very low ADI reflects this.
regulatory: USA: FDA revoked its authorisation for use in food in January 2025, with a deadline for manufacturers to reformulate.
EU: allowed only in a few specific products.

additives.name: Allura Red AC
additives.fssai: not on FSSAI's list of permitted synthetic colours at last review (check imported products)
additives.note: Synthetic red dye; one of the dyes in the UK hyperactivity study.
regulatory: EU: warning label about activity and attention in children required.

additives.name: Indigo carmine
additives.note: Synthetic blue dye.

additives.name: Brilliant Blue FCF
additives.note: Synthetic blue dye.

additives.name: Copper chlorophylls
additives.note: Green colour made from plant chlorophyll.

additives.name: Fast Green FCF
additives.note: Synthetic green dye.
regulatory: Not authorised as a food colour in the EU.

additives.name: Plain caramel
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Brown colour made by heating sugar.

additives.name: Caustic sulphite caramel
additives.note: Brown caramel colour.

additives.name: Ammonia caramel
additives.note: Brown colour. Can contain small amounts of 4-MEI, a by-product IARC lists as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B); levels in foods are regulated in some places.

additives.name: Sulphite ammonia caramel
additives.note: Brown colour common in colas and sauces. Can contain small amounts of 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B).

additives.name: Carotenes (beta-carotene)
additives.note: Orange colour; the body can turn it into vitamin A.

additives.name: Annatto extracts
additives.adi_note: separate ADIs for bixin and norbixin
additives.note: Natural orange colour from annatto seeds; rare allergic reactions.

additives.name: Paprika extract
additives.note: Natural red-orange colour from paprika.

additives.name: Beetroot red
additives.note: Natural red colour from beetroot.

additives.name: Calcium carbonate
additives.note: Also a source of calcium.

additives.name: Titanium dioxide
additives.adi_note: JECFA kept 'not specified' in 2023; EFSA concluded in 2021 it can no longer be considered safe as a food additive
additives.fssai: permitted in some categories (check current regulation)
additives.note: White pigment used in sweets, icing and chewing gum. Regulators disagree: the EU banned it in food in 2022 because possible genetic damage could not be ruled out; JECFA did not find a health concern at current intakes.
regulatory: EU: banned as a food additive since 2022.

additives.name: Sorbic acid
additives.note: Common, well-studied preservative against moulds and yeasts.

additives.name: Potassium sorbate
additives.note: Common, well-studied preservative against moulds and yeasts.

additives.name: Benzoic acid
additives.note: Preservative. In drinks that also contain vitamin C (ascorbic acid), small amounts of benzene can form with heat and light; manufacturers are expected to control this.

additives.name: Sodium benzoate
additives.note: Preservative common in soft drinks, sauces and pickles. Was part of the dye mixture in the UK hyperactivity study. With vitamin C in drinks, small amounts of benzene can form.

additives.name: Potassium benzoate
additives.note: Benzoate preservative; same group limit and notes as sodium benzoate (211).

additives.name: Calcium benzoate
additives.note: Benzoate preservative; same group limit and notes as sodium benzoate (211).

additives.name: Sulphur dioxide
additives.adi_source: JECFA (group ADI for sulphites, as SO2)
additives.fssai: permitted (limits apply); must be declared as an allergen above 10 mg/kg
additives.note: Sulphites can trigger breathing problems in some people with asthma.
regulatory: Must be declared on the label above 10 mg/kg in India and the EU.

additives.name: Sodium metabisulphite
additives.adi_source: JECFA (group ADI for sulphites, as SO2)
additives.fssai: permitted (limits apply); must be declared as an allergen above 10 mg/kg
additives.note: Sulphite preservative; can trigger breathing problems in some people with asthma.
regulatory: Must be declared on the label above 10 mg/kg in India and the EU.

additives.name: Potassium metabisulphite
additives.adi_source: JECFA (group ADI for sulphites, as SO2)
additives.fssai: permitted (limits apply); must be declared as an allergen above 10 mg/kg
additives.note: Sulphite preservative (common in squashes, pickles); can trigger breathing problems in some people with asthma.
regulatory: Must be declared on the label above 10 mg/kg in India and the EU.

additives.name: Nisin
additives.note: Natural antibacterial made by fermentation; used in processed cheese and some canned foods.

additives.name: Natamycin
additives.note: Anti-mould preservative used on cheese surfaces and some baked goods.

additives.name: Sodium nitrite
additives.fssai: permitted in specific meat products (limits apply)
additives.note: Keeps cured meat pink and prevents botulism, but can form nitrosamines in the gut and during high-heat cooking. Processed meat is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) for bowel cancer.

additives.name: Sodium nitrate
additives.note: Converts to nitrite; same concerns as nitrite in processed meats.

additives.name: Acetic acid
additives.note: The acid in vinegar.

additives.name: Sodium acetates
additives.note: Salt of acetic acid (vinegar); adds a little sodium.

additives.name: Calcium acetate
additives.note: Salt of acetic acid.

additives.name: Lactic acid
additives.note: Acid produced by fermentation (curd).

additives.name: Sodium propionate
additives.note: Mould inhibitor used in bread and bakery products.

additives.name: Calcium propionate
additives.note: Mould inhibitor used in bread and bakery products.

additives.name: Carbon dioxide
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: The fizz in carbonated drinks.

additives.name: Malic acid
additives.note: Fruit acid (apples).

additives.name: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C)
additives.note: Vitamin C, used to stop food going brown.

additives.name: Sodium ascorbate
additives.note: Salt form of vitamin C.

additives.name: Ascorbyl palmitate
additives.note: Fat-soluble form of vitamin C.

additives.name: Alpha-tocopherol (vitamin E)
additives.note: Vitamin E, used to stop fats going rancid.

additives.name: Propyl gallate
additives.note: Synthetic antioxidant for fats and oils; rare allergic reactions.

additives.name: Tertiary butylhydroquinone (TBHQ)
additives.fssai: permitted in fats, oils and some foods (limits apply)
additives.note: Synthetic antioxidant used to stop frying oils and snacks going rancid. Safe within the ADI, but heavy snack eaters can get close to it.
regulatory: EU and USA: permitted with limits (USA: no more than 0.02% of the fat or oil content).

additives.name: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA)
additives.note: Synthetic antioxidant. IARC lists it as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B), based on animal studies at high doses.

additives.name: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT)
additives.note: Synthetic antioxidant used in fats and cereals.

additives.name: Lecithins
additives.note: Natural emulsifier, usually from soy or sunflower. Soy lecithin can matter for people with severe soy allergy.

additives.name: Sodium lactate
additives.note: Salt of lactic acid.

additives.name: Calcium lactate
additives.note: Salt of lactic acid; also adds calcium.

additives.name: Citric acid
additives.note: Acid found naturally in lemons. In drinks, frequent sipping of acidic drinks can wear tooth enamel.

additives.name: Sodium citrates
additives.note: Salt of citric acid.

additives.name: Potassium citrates
additives.note: Salt of citric acid.

additives.name: Calcium citrates
additives.note: Salt of citric acid; also adds calcium.

additives.name: Tartaric acid
additives.note: Fruit acid (grapes, tamarind).

additives.name: Phosphoric acid
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus (JECFA uses a maximum tolerable daily intake of 70)
additives.note: Acid in colas; frequent intake wears tooth enamel. Phosphate additives are absorbed very easily, which matters for people with kidney disease.

additives.name: Sodium phosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive; adds sodium and highly absorbable phosphorus.

additives.name: Potassium phosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive; adds highly absorbable phosphorus and potassium.

additives.name: Calcium phosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive.

additives.name: Magnesium phosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive.

additives.name: Sodium alginate
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Thickener made from brown seaweed.

additives.name: Agar
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Seaweed-based gelling agent; a vegetarian alternative to gelatin.

additives.name: Carrageenan
additives.adi_note: not specified (JECFA); EFSA set a temporary group ADI of 75 mg/kg in 2018
additives.note: Seaweed-based thickener in dairy desserts and drinks. Some researchers question its effect on gut inflammation; regulators consider food-grade carrageenan safe within limits.

additives.name: Locust bean gum
additives.note: Plant-based thickener (a type of fibre).

additives.name: Guar gum
additives.note: Plant-based thickener (a type of fibre), largely produced in India.

additives.name: Gum arabic
additives.note: Natural gum from acacia trees.

additives.name: Xanthan gum
additives.note: Thickener made by fermentation.

additives.name: Gellan gum
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Made by fermentation; keeps particles suspended in drinks.

additives.name: Sorbitol
additives.note: Sugar alcohol. Large amounts can cause bloating and a laxative effect.

additives.name: Glycerol
additives.note: Keeps food moist.

additives.name: Konjac
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Plant fibre that forms a firm gel. Small konjac jelly cups have caused choking in children.
regulatory: EU: not allowed in jelly mini-cups because of the choking risk.

additives.name: Polysorbate 80
additives.note: Synthetic emulsifier. Mouse studies found gut-lining and gut-bacteria changes at high doses; human evidence is still limited.

additives.name: Pectin
additives.note: Natural fibre from fruit, used in jams.

additives.name: Brominated vegetable oil (BVO)
additives.note: Was used to keep flavour oils suspended in citrus drinks; bromine can build up in the body.
regulatory: USA: FDA revoked its authorisation in 2024.
Not authorised in the EU.

additives.name: Diphosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive common in baked goods and noodles.

additives.name: Triphosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive common in noodles and processed meat.

additives.name: Polyphosphates
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Phosphate additive.

additives.name: Cellulose
additives.note: Plant fibre.

additives.name: Methyl cellulose
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Plant-fibre based thickener; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC)
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Plant-fibre based thickener, also used for vegetarian capsules.

additives.name: Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)
additives.note: Thickener. A small human trial found it changed gut bacteria; long-term health effects are unknown.

additives.name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
aliases: mono and di-glycerides of fatty acids
additives.note: Very common emulsifier. Large French observational studies (NutriNet-Santé) linked higher intake of this emulsifier with higher heart disease and cancer risk; this shows an association, not proof of harm.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from plant oils or animal fat; the label rarely says which.

additives.name: Citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
aliases: citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
additives.note: Emulsifier used in fats and infant formula.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from plant or animal fat.

additives.name: DATEM
aliases: diacetyl tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
additives.note: Dough strengthener used in bread.

additives.name: Polyglycerol esters of fatty acids
additives.note: Emulsifier used in cakes and whipped toppings.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from plant or animal fat.

additives.name: Polyglycerol polyricinoleate (PGPR)
additives.note: Lets manufacturers use less cocoa butter in chocolate.

additives.name: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids
aliases: propylene glycol esters of fatty acids
additives.note: Emulsifier used in cakes and toppings.

additives.name: Sodium stearoyl lactylate (SSL)
additives.note: Dough conditioner used in bread and biscuits.

additives.name: Sorbitan monostearate
additives.note: Emulsifier used in yeast, cakes and toppings.

additives.name: Sorbitan tristearate
additives.note: Emulsifier used in chocolate and compound coatings.

additives.name: Sodium carbonates (incl. baking soda)
additives.note: Baking soda. Adds a little sodium.

additives.name: Potassium carbonates
additives.note: Used in noodles and baking.

additives.name: Ammonium carbonates
additives.note: Raising agent in biscuits; turns into gas during baking.

additives.name: Magnesium carbonates
additives.note: Keeps powders and salt free-flowing.

additives.name: Potassium chloride
additives.note: Used to replace part of the salt. People with kidney disease or on some blood-pressure medicines may need to limit potassium.

additives.name: Calcium sulphate
additives.note: Used in bread and to set tofu; adds calcium.

additives.name: Sodium ferrocyanide
additives.note: Keeps table salt free-flowing. The compound is very stable and does not release harmful cyanide at permitted levels.

additives.name: Potassium ferrocyanide
additives.note: Keeps table salt free-flowing. The compound is very stable and does not release harmful cyanide at permitted levels.

additives.name: Sodium aluminium phosphate
additives.adi_note: Aluminium from all sources: JECFA tolerable weekly intake 2 mg/kg body weight (EFSA: 1 mg/kg per week)
additives.note: Raising agent that contains aluminium. High aluminium intake from all sources can affect the nervous system and bones; young children who eat a lot of baked goods can exceed the safe weekly intake.
regulatory: EU: since Regulation 380/2012, allowed only in Battenberg-type sponge cakes, to cut aluminium intake.

additives.name: Bone phosphate
additives.adi_note: EFSA group ADI for phosphates, as phosphorus
additives.note: Calcium phosphate made from animal bones.

additives.name: Silicon dioxide
additives.note: Keeps powders free-flowing.

additives.name: Sodium aluminosilicate
additives.adi_note: Aluminium from all sources: JECFA tolerable weekly intake 2 mg/kg body weight (EFSA: 1 mg/kg per week)
additives.note: Anti-caking agent in salt and powders; contains aluminium.
regulatory: EU: use restricted by Regulation 380/2012 to cut aluminium intake.

additives.name: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
additives.adi_note: not specified (JECFA); EFSA set a group ADI of 30 mg/kg as glutamic acid in 2017
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label must state it
additives.note: Adds savoury taste. Studies have not confirmed the popular 'MSG symptom' reactions, but it adds sodium, and its presence usually signals a heavily processed, salty food.

additives.name: Disodium guanylate
additives.note: Savoury flavour enhancer usually used with MSG. Contains purines, which people with gout are often told to limit.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from fish or meat, or by fermentation; check for a green veg mark.

additives.name: Disodium inosinate
additives.note: Savoury flavour enhancer usually used with MSG. Contains purines.
additives.animal_note: Often made from fish or meat; check for a green veg mark.

additives.name: Disodium 5'-ribonucleotides
additives.note: Mix of 627 and 631. Contains purines.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from fish or meat, or by fermentation; check for a green veg mark.

additives.name: Dimethylpolysiloxane
additives.note: Silicone anti-foam added to frying oil; common in instant noodles and fried snacks.

additives.name: Beeswax
additives.note: Shiny coating on sweets and fruit.
additives.animal_note: Made by bees: usually fine for vegetarians, not vegan.

additives.name: Carnauba wax
additives.note: Shiny coating on sweets.

additives.name: Shellac
additives.note: Shiny coating from lac insects (not vegan).
additives.animal_note: Made by lac insects: not vegan.

additives.name: L-cysteine
additives.adi_note: acceptable for use as a flour treatment agent
additives.note: Dough conditioner used in bread and biscuits.
additives.animal_note: Can be made from feathers or hair, or by fermentation.

additives.name: Potassium bromate
additives.adi_note: no ADI — not considered safe for use
additives.note: Bread improver that caused cancer in animal studies. If you see this on an Indian product, report it to FSSAI.
regulatory: Banned in India (2016), the EU, the UK and many other countries.

additives.name: Azodicarbonamide
additives.note: Bread dough conditioner; can break down into semicarbazide during baking. Mainly a breathing hazard for workers handling the powder.
regulatory: Not authorised in the EU.

additives.name: Acesulfame potassium
additives.adi_source: JECFA (EFSA raised its ADI to 15 in 2025)
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label warning required
additives.note: Zero-calorie sweetener. Regulators consider it safe within the ADI. WHO advises against relying on non-sugar sweeteners for weight control.

additives.name: Aspartame
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label warnings required
additives.note: In 2023 IARC classed it as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B, limited evidence), while JECFA kept the same ADI of 40 mg/kg — so normal intake is considered safe. Contains phenylalanine, which people with phenylketonuria (PKU) must avoid.
regulatory: Label must warn people with phenylketonuria.

additives.name: Cyclamates
additives.note: Non-sugar sweetener.
regulatory: Not permitted in food in the USA since 1969.

additives.name: Isomalt
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Sugar alcohol in 'sugar-free' sweets; large amounts can cause a laxative effect.

additives.name: Saccharin
additives.adi_source: JECFA (EFSA raised its ADI to 9 in 2024)
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label warning required
additives.note: Oldest non-sugar sweetener. Earlier cancer concerns came from rat studies not relevant to humans.

additives.name: Sucralose
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label warning required
additives.note: Zero-calorie sweetener. Considered safe within the ADI; some newer lab studies (not yet confirmed in people) raised questions, and heating it to baking temperatures is not recommended.

additives.name: Steviol glycosides
additives.note: Sweetener from the stevia plant.

additives.name: Neotame
additives.note: Very intense sweetener related to aspartame.

additives.name: Aspartame-acesulfame salt
additives.adi_note: covered by the ADIs of aspartame (40) and acesulfame K (15)
additives.fssai: permitted in specific categories; label warnings required
additives.note: A combined sweetener that releases aspartame and acesulfame K. Contains phenylalanine, which people with phenylketonuria (PKU) must avoid.
regulatory: Label must warn people with phenylketonuria.

additives.name: Maltitol
additives.note: Sugar alcohol in 'sugar-free' sweets. It still raises blood sugar somewhat and can cause a laxative effect.

additives.name: Lactitol
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Sugar alcohol made from milk sugar; laxative in large amounts.

additives.name: Xylitol
additives.note: Sugar alcohol; kinder to teeth than sugar; laxative in large amounts.

additives.name: Erythritol
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Sugar alcohol in 'sugar-free' and keto products. A 2023 observational study linked high blood erythritol levels with heart attack and stroke; this is not yet confirmed.

additives.name: Advantame
additives.note: Very intense sweetener related to aspartame.

additives.name: Amylases
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Enzyme that helps bread rise and stay soft.

additives.name: Oxidised starch
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Monostarch phosphate
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Distarch phosphate
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Acetylated distarch phosphate
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Acetylated starch
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Acetylated distarch adipate
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Hydroxypropyl starch
additives.adi_note: not specified (no safety concern at normal use)
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Starch sodium octenyl succinate
additives.note: Chemically modified starch; a marker of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Propylene glycol
additives.note: Carrier for flavours.
